title: Where the next edge comes from

lede.technical: Four research paths ordered by cost of evidence — each builds on the evaluation loop the system already has, and each is gated by the one before it.
lede.plain: Four ways to find strategies that actually work, ordered from cheapest to most expensive to test. Each one only makes sense after the one before it is proven.

paths.title: Macro Economic Premia & Cross-Sectional Baskets
paths.summary: Exploiting slow fundamental yield spreads, central bank policy divergence, and cross-sectional currency momentum across the 8-major basket (H-01, H-02, H-03, H-11, H-12).
paths.evidence: Point-in-time collectors for FRED, BIS policy rates, and official central bank yields (ECB, BoC, MoF, US Treasury) live in src/research/collectors.

paths.title: Weak-Voters Committee Ensemble (H-20261019-04)
paths.summary: Combining weak, lowly-correlated signals at equal risk. Rather than seeking a single elusive high-Sharpe indicator, aggregate diverse economic and flow voters into a diversified book.
paths.evidence: Registered card H-20261019-04 rated PROMISING in trial ledger. Proven superior to single-pair indicators under conservative bid/ask replay.

paths.title: Institutional Positioning & Flow Premia
paths.summary: CFTC Traders in Financial Futures (TFF / COT) asset-manager flow (H-15) and quarter-end corporate rebalancing flows (H-19).
paths.evidence: CFTC collector ingesting weekly positioning; tested against friction markup.

paths.title: Execution Friction, Financing Drag & Go-Live Hardening
paths.summary: Empirical measurement of OANDA financing markup (1.1%/yr drag), dynamic spread guards, priceBound slippage limits, and daily rollover hold.
paths.evidence: Deployed in pin 17827c5 on 2026-10-18 across System 2 and System 3.

paths.title: Single-Pair Technical Indicator Optimization (Legacy 67)
paths.summary: Moving average crossovers, Donchian channels, and Bollinger break-outs on single currency pairs.
paths.evidence: Cards H-20261019-01, H-20261019-02, H-20261019-03 backtested under honest friction standard and systematically KILLED. Retired from active scope.

body.technical: The ordering is deliberate: each path is gated by evidence from the one before it. Path 1 (cost calibration) changes what passes the existing gates without changing any strategy code — it is pure measurement and should take days. Path 2 (lower timeframes) is the highest-leverage new strategy work but depends on correct costs. Path 3 (session conditioning) is a free option on the existing strategy set. Path 4 (NLP) is the owner's stated vision and the destination, but it carries the most integration risk and should prove its evaluation loop on paths that are cheaper to get wrong.
body.plain: Do them in order. The first one is cheap and changes the picture immediately. The second one adds the most new trading opportunities. The third one is free — it just narrows when things trade. The fourth one is the big one, and you earn the right to attempt it by proving the testing process on the first three.
